edges.description: Early somatic SF3B1 mutations establish a founder hematopoietic stem cell clone in MDS.
Mutant SF3B1 alters 3'-splice site recognition and induces widespread aberrant pre-mRNA splicing.
SF3B1 spliceosome mutations specifically drive perinuclear mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts (ring sideroblasts).

edges.description: Early somatic DNMT3A mutations confer clonal dominance across the marrow hematopoietic compartment.
Methyltransferase-domain DNMT3A mutations alter CpG DNA methylation landscapes in clonal myeloid progenitors.

edges.description: TET2 inactivation arises in hematopoietic stem cells and drives aberrant stem-cell self-renewal and clonal expansion.
Loss of TET2 dioxygenase activity impairs 5-methylcytosine oxidation and causes a DNA hypermethylation phenotype.

edges.description: Somatic ASXL1 loss expands the hematopoietic stem/progenitor pool while impairing mature myeloid differentiation.
ASXL1 loss impairs Polycomb repressive chromatin modification (global H3K27me3 reduction) and dysregulates hematopoietic transcriptional programs.

edges.description: Dominant clonal MDS stem cells generate dysplastic myeloid progenitors that fail terminal maturation.
Clonal hematopoietic stem cells acquire cooperating driver mutations that promote subclonal progression toward acute myeloid leukemia.
Abnormal pre-mRNA splicing compromises myeloid and erythroid differentiation and maturation.
Epigenetic silencing of hematopoietic differentiation programs impairs myeloid maturation.

evidence.snippet: Somatic Addition of Sex Combs Like 1 (ASXL1) mutations occur in 10-30% of patients with myeloid malignancies, most commonly in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDSs), and are associated with adverse outcome.

nodes.description: Disrupted CpG methylation/demethylation balance and Polycomb chromatin modification produce promoter DNA hypermethylation and epigenetic silencing of lineage-differentiation and tumor-suppressor programs in clonal MDS progenitors, providing the pharmacologic substrate targeted by hypomethylating agents.

biological_processes: negative regulation of gene expression via chromosomal CpG island methylation

evidence.reference_title: Decitabine improves patient outcomes in myelodysplastic syndromes: results of a phase III randomized study.
evidence.snippet: Aberrant DNA methylation, which results in leukemogenesis, is frequent in patients with myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and is a potential target for pharmacologic therapy. Decitabine indirectly depletes methylcytosine and causes hypomethylation of target gene promoters.

evidence.reference_title: Restoration of TET2 Function Blocks Aberrant Self-Renewal and Leukemia Progression.
evidence.snippet: Loss-of-function mutations in TET2 occur frequently in patients with clonal hematopoiesis, myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), and acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and are associated with a DNA hypermethylation phenotype.

nodes.description: Mutant 3'-splice site spliceosome complexes misrecognize branchpoints and exonic splicing enhancers across hundreds of hematopoietic transcripts, generating mis-spliced isoforms and nonsense-mediated mRNA decay that impair erythroid and myeloid maturation.

evidence.reference_title: Frequent pathway mutations of splicing machinery in myelodysplasia.
evidence.snippet: most of the mutations, which occurred in a mutually exclusive manner, affected genes involved in the 3'-splice site recognition during pre-mRNA processing, inducing abnormal RNA splicing and compromised haematopoiesis.

nodes.description: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the only potentially curative therapy for MDS, used primarily in eligible higher-risk patients.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Myelodysplastic Syndromes: A Review.
evidence.snippet: Hematopoietic cell transplantation is potentially curative and should be considered for patients with higher-risk MDS at the time of diagnosis.

nodes.description: Reduced red cell mass from ineffective erythropoiesis is the most common presenting cytopenia in MDS, causing fatigue, pallor, and frequently transfusion dependence.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and biological implications of driver mutations in myelodysplastic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) are a heterogeneous group of chronic hematological malignancies characterized by dysplasia, ineffective hematopoiesis

nodes.description: Azacitidine is a hypomethylating agent (DNA methyltransferase inhibitor) that prolongs overall survival and delays AML transformation in higher-risk MDS compared with conventional care regimens.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of azacitidine compared with that of conventional care regimens in the treatment of higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes: a randomised, open-label, phase III study.
evidence.snippet: Treatment with azacitidine prolongs overall survival and lowers the risk of progression to acute myeloid leukaemia in patients with higher-risk myelodysplastic syndrome

nodes.description: Multi-hit (biallelic) somatic inactivation of TP53 disables DNA-damage checkpoint surveillance in hematopoietic stem cells, driving complex karyotype chromosomal instability, therapy resistance, and rapid leukemic transformation.
nodes.id: Biallelic TP53 Inactivation and Genomic Instability

evidence.reference_title: Implications of TP53 allelic state for genome stability, clinical presentation and outcomes in myelodysplastic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Established associations with complex karyotype, few co-occurring mutations, high-risk presentation and poor outcomes were specific to multi-hit patients only.

nodes.description: Acquisition of additional cooperating mutations and outgrowth of aggressive subclones drive progression of MDS to acute myeloid leukemia. Leukemia-free survival deteriorates progressively as the number of driver mutations increases, and the risk is greatest in higher-risk, increased-blast disease.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and biological implications of driver mutations in myelodysplastic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: leukemia-free survival deteriorated steadily as numbers of driver mutations increased.

nodes.description: MDS originates in a hematopoietic stem cell that acquires recurrent somatic driver mutations, establishing a dominant neoplastic clone in the bone marrow that displaces normal polyclonal hematopoiesis.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and biological implications of driver mutations in myelodysplastic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Seventy-eight percent of patients had 1 or more oncogenic mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrent DNMT3A mutations in patients with myelodysplastic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: we report the frequency of DNMT3A mutations in patients with de novo MDS, and their association with secondary AML.

nodes.description: Decitabine (5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine) is a hypomethylating agent used in higher-risk MDS, reversing aberrant DNA methylation to restore myeloid differentiation.

evidence.reference_title: Decitabine improves patient outcomes in myelodysplastic syndromes: results of a phase III randomized study.
evidence.snippet: Decitabine was found to be clinically effective in the treatment of patients with MDS, provided durable responses, and improved time to AML transformation or death.

nodes.description: Iron-laden mitochondria forming a perinuclear ring in erythroblasts (ring sideroblasts) characterize SF3B1-mutant MDS with ring sideroblasts.
nodes.id: Elevated Bone Marrow Ring Sideroblast Count

evidence.reference_title: SF3B1-mutant MDS as a distinct disease subtype: a proposal from the International Working Group for the Prognosis of MDS.
evidence.snippet: SF3B1 mutation identifies a condition characterized by ring sideroblasts (RS), ineffective erythropoiesis, and indolent clinical course.

nodes.description: Recombinant erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (epoetin alfa and darbepoetin alfa) are standard first-line therapy for symptomatic anemia in lower-risk MDS, particularly in patients with serum erythropoietin below 200 to 500 U/L, reducing red-cell transfusion requirements.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of luspatercept versus epoetin alfa in erythropoiesis-stimulating agent-naive, transfusion-dependent, lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (COMMANDS): interim analysis of a phase 3, open-label, randomised controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) are the standard-of-care treatment for anaemia in most patients with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes but responses are limited and transient.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of luspatercept versus epoetin alfa in erythropoiesis-stimulating agent-naive, transfusion-dependent, lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (COMMANDS): interim analysis of a phase 3, open-label, randomised controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: 86 (59%) of 147 patients in the luspatercept group and 48 (31%) of 154 patients in the epoetin alfa group reached the primary endpoint (common risk difference on response rate 26·6; 95% CI 15·8-37·4; p<0·0001).

nodes.description: Imetelstat is a competitive oligonucleotide telomerase inhibitor approved for red-cell transfusion-dependent lower-risk MDS relapsed, refractory, or ineligible for erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, achieving durable transfusion independence in the Phase III IMerge trial.

evidence.reference_title: Imetelstat in patients with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes who have relapsed or are refractory to erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (IMerge): a multinational, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
evidence.snippet: In the imetelstat group, 47 (40% [95% CI 30·9-49·3]) patients had an RBC-TI of at least 8 weeks versus nine (15% [7·1-26·6]) in the placebo group

nodes.description: Dysplastic clonal progenitors undergo accelerated intramedullary apoptosis and fail to mature normally, producing a paradox of hypercellular or normocellular marrow with peripheral blood cytopenias. Ineffective erythropoiesis is the dominant lesion in many lower-risk subtypes, manifesting as anemia.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and biological implications of driver mutations in myelodysplastic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) are a heterogeneous group of chronic hematological malignancies characterized by dysplasia, ineffective hematopoiesis

nodes.description: Oral iron chelation therapy (deferasirox) is used alongside chronic red-cell transfusion support in lower-risk MDS to manage transfusional iron overload.

evidence.reference_title: Myelodysplastic Syndromes: New Methods of Diagnosis, Prognostication, and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: Low-risk patients are treated supportively with erythrocyte transfusions and iron chelation therapy.

nodes.description: Ivosidenib is an oral mutant isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (mIDH1) inhibitor approved for adult patients with relapsed or refractory IDH1-mutated MDS, inducing durable complete remissions and transfusion independence.

evidence.reference_title: Final phase 1 substudy results of ivosidenib for patients with mutant IDH1 relapsed/refractory myelodysplastic syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Rates of CR + PR and objective response (CR + PR + marrow CR) were 38.9% (95% confidence interval [CI], 17.3-64.3) and 83.3% (95% CI, 58.6-96.4), respectively.

nodes.description: Lenalidomide reduces transfusion requirements and induces cytogenetic responses in MDS with isolated del(5q), suppressing the abnormal 5q- clone.

evidence.reference_title: Lenalidomide in the myelodysplastic syndrome with chromosome 5q deletion.
evidence.snippet: Lenalidomide can reduce transfusion requirements and reverse cytologic and cytogenetic abnormalities in patients who have the myelodysplastic syndrome with the 5q31 deletion.

nodes.description: Luspatercept is a recombinant fusion protein (erythroid maturation agent) that reduces anemia and red-cell transfusion dependence in lower-risk MDS, both in ESA-naive transfusion-dependent patients (COMMANDS) and in ring-sideroblast lower-risk MDS refractory to erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (MEDALIST).

evidence.reference_title: Luspatercept in Patients with Lower-Risk Myelodysplastic Syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Transfusion independence for 8 weeks or longer was observed in 38% of the patients in the luspatercept group, as compared with 13% of those in the placebo group

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of luspatercept versus epoetin alfa in erythropoiesis-stimulating agent-naive, transfusion-dependent, lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (COMMANDS): interim analysis of a phase 3, open-label, randomised controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: In this interim analysis, luspatercept improved the rate at which red blood cell transfusion independence and increased haemoglobin were achieved compared with epoetin alfa in ESA-naive patients with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes.

nodes.description: Morphologic dysplasia in one or more myeloid lineages (dyserythropoiesis, dysgranulopoiesis, dysmegakaryopoiesis) is the defining marrow finding of MDS.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical effect of point mutations in myelodysplastic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: In a multivariable Cox regression model, the presence of mutations in five genes retained independent prognostic significance: TP53 (hazard ratio for death from any cause, 2.48; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.60 to 3.84), EZH2 (hazard ratio, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.36 to 3.33), ETV6 (hazard ratio, 2.04; 95% CI, 1.08 to 3.86), RUNX1 (hazard ratio, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.01 to 2.15), and ASXL1 (hazard ratio, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.00 to 1.89).

nodes.description: Early somatic heterozygous mutations in DNMT3A (most commonly at R882 in the methyltransferase domain) impair de novo CpG DNA methyltransferase activity in clonal hematopoietic stem cells and accelerate progression to secondary AML.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrent DNMT3A mutations in patients with myelodysplastic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Amino acid R882, located in the methyltransferase domain of DNMT3A, was the most common mutation site, accounting for 4/13 mutations. DNMT3A mutations were expressed in the majority of cells in all tested mutant samples regardless of myeloblast counts, suggesting that DNMT3A mutations occur early in the course of MDS.

nodes.description: Somatic founder mutations in the core 3'-splice site recognition factor SF3B1 alter branchpoint and 3'-splice site selection during pre-mRNA processing in hematopoietic stem cells, driving aberrant splicing, mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts (ring sideroblasts), and ineffective erythropoiesis.

nodes.description: Mutually exclusive somatic mutations in the 3'-splice site recognition factors SRSF2 and U2AF1 (U2AF35) alter exonic splicing enhancer and 3'-AG dinucleotide recognition in hematopoietic stem cells, driving aberrant pre-mRNA splicing and multilineage myeloid dysplasia without the SF3B1-characteristic ring-sideroblast phenotype.

nodes.description: Recurrent somatic loss-of-function mutations and deletions in TET2 impair 5-methylcytosine dioxygenase-mediated DNA demethylation in hematopoietic stem cells, producing a DNA hypermethylation phenotype and clonal stem-cell self-renewal advantage in MDS.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in TET2 in myeloid cancers.
